title: NDVI — Normalized Difference Vegetation Index

NDVI.description: Vegetation index (-1 to +1; >0.3 = vegetation; >0.6 = dense/healthy vegetation)

applicability: Anomalous NDVI on dam/levee surfaces indicates moisture concentration from seepage. Compare to baseline seasonal pattern. Threshold: NDVI > 0.15–0.20 on surfaces expected to be bare/dry suggests seepage influence.
source: Rouse et al. (1974), general remote sensing

title: Stefan-Boltzmann Law — Radiant Exitance

M.description: Radiant exitance (thermal radiation power per area)

ε.description: Surface emissivity (0.90–0.98 for soil, water, concrete, vegetation)

applicability: Thermal cameras measure radiant exitance and convert to apparent temperature. Emissivity correction essential — water ε ≈ 0.96, dry soil ε ≈ 0.92–0.96, concrete ε ≈ 0.90–0.95, vegetation ε ≈ 0.95–0.98. At 20°C, 1°C change ≈ 5 W/m² change in exitance.

title: Thermal Contrast for Seepage Detection

ΔT.description: Temperature difference between seepage zone and dry surface

T_seepage.description: Surface temperature at seepage zone (influenced by reservoir temperature)

T_dry.description: Surface temperature of dry (non-seepage) adjacent area

applicability: ΔT typically 2–10°C in optimal conditions (pre-dawn, cool season). Minimum detectable ΔT: 0.1°C (cooled sensors) to 0.5°C (uncooled). Best in winter/spring when reservoir water is warmer than ambient. Summer: contrast may reverse or diminish.

title: GB-InSAR Displacement Precision

SNR.description: Signal-to-noise ratio (typically 20–40 dB for dam surfaces)

applicability: Practical precision: 0.1–0.5 mm for individual measurements at typical dam ranges (100–2000 m). Atmospheric correction critical — path length errors of 1–10 mm common. Differential measurement relative to stable reference reflectors mitigates atmospheric effects.

title: Corner Reflector Radar Cross Section (RCS)

a.description: Inner edge length of triangular corner reflector

applicability: RCS scales as a⁴ — doubling edge length increases RCS by 16×. For C-band satellite InSAR (λ=0.056 m): a=0.7 m gives RCS ≈ 34 dBm², sufficient for reliable PS identification. Multiple corner reflectors on dam crest/face create known reference points.

title: Seepage Velocity from Thermal Profile (Bredehoeft & Papadopulos)
equation: T(z) = T_s + (T_d - T_s) × [exp(v_z × z / κ) - 1] / [exp(v_z × L / κ) - 1]

κ.description: Thermal diffusivity of saturated soil (~0.5–1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m²/s)

applicability: 1D steady-state conduction-advection model. Deviation of temperature profile from linear (conduction-only) indicates vertical groundwater flow. Concave-up profile = downward flow; convex-up = upward flow. Applied using DTS (Distributed Temperature Sensing) in monitoring boreholes.
